title: Add an audience-check role that rates the live explainer page
summary: Add a second recorded role, "audience", beside the steward. It reads the live firstmate explainer page as a newcomer and writes a 1–5 rating with findings as a record. The steward's brief and `athena status` then show that record. The audience is the steward and owner, who judge whether shipped outcomes work for their readers.

defaults_applied.how: The new role, record and wiring get unit and integration tests. Clippy and fmt stay clean.
All code is Rust, in the existing crates.
Rating range and evidence requirements are enforced by record validation, not by prose.
Behavior is checked by running cargo test, which exercises the role end to end with the fake agent.
The docs page and CHANGELOG entry are written for an outside reader.
Records contain only the page URL, ratings and cited findings.
One focused role with one target; further targets are deferred.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The explainer's live URL comes from the existing Pages deployment (`xtask/src/site.rs`, `.github/workflows/pages.yml`, README line ~134). It is configurable and not hard-coded to an owner name.

The role runs through the existing agent and role machinery, like the steward. Its fetch of the page goes through the agent's allowed read tools. Tests use the fake agent and a stub page, never the real network.
A new role needs no change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows. I assumed cadence and target can live in the role definition and code.
The earlier ratings of 2/5 from outside Athena are not imported. Only new ratings are recorded.
The role may be triggered by a CLI command and by cadence. Choosing between the two is left to the producer, who keeps the change small.

acceptance_criteria.text: An `audience` role definition exists in roles.rs, with a goal, a short stable prompt and a cadence. The prompt tells the role to read the outcome as its audience would, give a 1–5 rating, and cite evidence for every finding. It validates under RoleDefinition::validate, and its path is records/roles/audience-<n>.json.

A versioned, schema-tagged record type holds the audited target (the explainer page URL), the audience (newcomer), the rating (1–5 only), findings that each cite a source, and the time. Out-of-range ratings and findings without evidence are refused.

Run `cargo test`. Tests pass for the role definition, the record's validation and round-trip, and an end-to-end run with the fake agent. That run produces a rating record from a stubbed page without network access and shows it to the steward. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.

Run `cargo test`. A test shows the steward's brief, or `athena status` output, includes the latest audience rating and findings. A rating at or below 2 produces a steward work item, so the owner can see the 2/5 result inside Athena.

The role reads and records only; it changes no code or docs. The record contains no secrets or personal data. The default target is the live explainer URL, configured in one place and not hard-coded in several.
A docs page and a CHANGELOG entry describe the role, how to run it, where its records go, and how to add a target beyond the explainer.

out_of_scope: Fixing the explainer page's content or design
Auditing outcomes other than the explainer, beyond a target field that allows them later
Importing the three earlier external ratings
Changes to the scoring rules, ladder or steward's limits
Changes to deploy workflows or Pages settings
departures: This is a larger multi-crate feature than the typical job: a new role, a new record type, wiring and tests. I raised cost and time, and lowered the verification pass chance.
